headline: High-risk shared-write and data-flow overlap: ECC and Replit Agent can both modify the same workspace and propagate unverified outputs into downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write filesystem, use MCP, and run browsers; Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files and acts inside the Repl with user checkpoints. A shared workspace or copied files create a plausible prompt-injection bridge, though no direct default channel is documented. The interaction is possible but not proven.
conditions: IF outputs from ECC are copied into Replit workspace files without sanitization
IF Replit Agent reads attacker-controlled file content as instructions
mitigations: Keep agent outputs in separate directories
Strip instructions from imported text files
Use a human review step before copying content
Disable MCP paths that ingest untrusted files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, learned skills, hooks, and security findings; Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. If they share a workspace or files are transferred between them, sensitive material can flow from one agent to the other. The profiles do not prove a default shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the same codebase or secrets-bearing files are accessible to both agents
IF ECC session artifacts are imported into a Replit workspace
mitigations: Separate secrets from shared project files
Move sensitive artifacts out of shared folders
Review file transfers before syncing
Rotate any secrets exposed in shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have execute_shell, install_packages, modify_git_state, read_filesystem, and write_filesystem. ECC also supports multiple instances with shared-state warnings, while Replit Agent persists filesystem across sessions. If both operate on the same repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state by default unless explicitly coordinated.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace
IF both modify git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign one agent per branch
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Review git diffs before commits
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC produces security findings, documentation, and code-related outputs; Replit Agent can act inside a Repl with user checkpoints. If Replit consumes ECC output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code or deployment changes. The checkpointing reduces but does not eliminate the risk, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses ECC-generated findings or code without verification
IF ECC output is treated as authoritative for deployment changes
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of ECC outputs
Compare outputs against source files before acting
Limit Replit actions to draft mode
Ask for explicit confirmation before deployment edits
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles security findings, hooks, and session artifacts; Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If regulated or sensitive data is moved between them, residency and retention policies may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a compliance-gap risk rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Replit Secrets or ECC session artifacts
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts
Document retention for session files
Delete stale session exports promptly
Keep deployment secrets out of ECC outputs
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
